data.exact_reserve_text: Losses and loss adjustment expenses are GBP 35.6m higher than 2015 resulting in an increase in the loss ratio from 54.3% to 67.3%. The main driver for the increase is due to adverse prior year development of GBP 10.3m as compared to GBP 9.3m favorable prior year development during the same period in 2015. The adverse development in 2016 is mainly attributable to the Personal Accident line of business which during 2016 booked losses from prior years (GBP 6.0m). There were also prior year losses in Property and DUAL Australia that contributed to the higher loss ratio.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Booked losses from prior years in the Personal Accident line
Prior year losses in Property contributed to higher loss ratio
Prior year losses in DUAL Australia contributed to higher loss ratio

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2016 the Syndicate's gross claims outstanding were GBP 223.495m. During 2016 there was net adverse prior-year reserve development of approximately GBP 9.38m (a strengthening of c.4.2% of opening gross reserves), driven mainly by adverse development in prior underwriting years. Management attribute the movement principally to prior-year losses in the Personal Accident portfolio (c.GBP 6.0m) with additional contributions from Property and DUAL Australia. The triangle gross development and the narrative both indicate an adverse/prior-year strengthening, though the narrative cites an adverse amount of GBP 10.3m (minor difference to the triangle-derived GBP 9.38m).
raw_causal_phrases: adverse prior year development of GBP 10.3m
prior year losses in Property and DUAL Australia

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development was computed from the gross claims development triangle (Technical Provisions note, page 44). The Managing Agent's narrative (page 2) states an adverse prior year development of GBP 10.3m; the triangle-based calculation gives GBP 9.38m (gross) - small discrepancy likely rounding/presentation and/or net/gross wording in the narrative. The triangle and balance sheet are in GBP 000 units; all triangle values were read from the gross triangle and converted to millions. No specific named catastrophe events were identified as drivers; some amounts (Property, DUAL Australia) are described but not quantified.
